newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen higher ahead of long weekend.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen higher ahead of long weekend.

text.p: Singapore shares are expected to tick up a little on Thursday after another stronger close on Wall Street overnight, dealers said.
New York's Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 92.71 points higher on Wednesday at 6,679.87.
Dealers said New York's rise, which followed a 135-point jump on Tuesday, was likely to stem negative sentiment in the Singapore market, which hit a 25-month low of 2,027.11 on Tuesday.
Singapore's benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended at 2,040.19 points on Wednesday, up 7.22.
The market was also likely to firm on book-squaring ahead of the long-weekend in Singapore. Friday is a public holiday.

They said early attention was likely to focus on property and steel group Lion Teck Chiang, which begins trading on Thursday. The firm said on Wednesday its initial public offering (IPO) of shares was 2.9 times subscribed but only 78 percent of its restricted offer, to existing shareholders, was taken up.
